name: Indiana
headline_status: Marijuana is illegal in Indiana for both recreational and medical use; only low-THC CBD products are allowed.
summary: Indiana has no medical or adult-use marijuana program, and simple possession is a criminal misdemeanor. CBD with no more than 0.3% THC has been legal since 2018. A 2026 bill to restrict intoxicating hemp products (SB 250) passed the Senate but died in the House, so delta-8 and similar products remain unregulated, with no age limit, even as a federal hemp THC cap approaches (most of it takes effect on 11 December 2026). Sen. Mike Bohacek plans to file a medical marijuana bill in 2027.

possession_limit.value: No amount of marijuana is legal to possess.

penalties.value: Simple possession is a Class B misdemeanor (up to 180 days and $1,000). With a prior drug conviction it becomes a Class A misdemeanor under 30 grams (up to 1 year, $5,000) or a felony at 30 grams or more.

medical_program.value: None. Indiana is among the few states with no medical marijuana program; Gov. Mike Braun has said he is open to discussing it but has not acted.

retail_sales.value: No legal marijuana sales of any kind.

hemp_thc.value: CBD with up to 0.3% THC has been legal since 2018. Intoxicating hemp products such as delta-8 and THCA are unregulated with no state age limit after SB 250 died in 2026.

regulator.value: No cannabis regulator. The Indiana Board of Pharmacy must review any finalized federal rescheduling and recommend whether the state should follow.

timeline.event: Law signed allowing sale and possession of CBD oil with up to 0.3% THC
Senate passes SB 250 (35-15) to set a 21+ age limit and rules for hemp THC; the House never takes it up
Board of Pharmacy reviews the federal rescheduling notice and takes no action
Federal hemp THC limits take effect, creating a conflict with Indiana's unregulated hemp market

pending.item: Sen. Mike Bohacek is drafting a 2027 bill to legalize and tax medical marijuana (not recreational).
pending.status: Being drafted; 2027 bills cannot be filed until late 2026
